about: The book's glossary (Companion/Glossary.lean renders it; scripts/check-glossary.py checks it). Each entry: id (the anchor, unique), tex (the symbol, written with the Gray Paper v0.8.1 macros of gp-macros.json), name (a few words), meaning (plain English; `...` is code, $...$ is maths), model (full Lean names, each linked to its API page; may be empty, then modelNote says why), place (a key of places: the book section that defines it). Text must be true of GP v0.8.1 and of the model.

sections.intro: The state $\thestate$ is everything the chain remembers between blocks. The paper splits it into the components below and writes a component's value after the block with a prime ($\activeset'$ is the active validator set after the block). Lowercase subscripts name parts of a component.

entries.name: the state
entries.meaning: The whole chain state: the tuple of all the components below.

entries.name: authorizer pools
entries.meaning: For each core, up to $\Cauthpoolsize$ authorizer hashes: the authorizers a work package may currently use to claim that core.

entries.name: authorizer queues
entries.meaning: For each core, $\Cauthqueuesize$ authorizer hashes that refill the pool, one per block, chosen by the timeslot. Its glyph is $\phi$, a circle with a straight stroke through it; the PVM registers use the other phi, $\varphi$, drawn as an open loop.

entries.name: recent history
entries.meaning: A log of recent activity, $(\recenthistory, \accoutbelt)$.

entries.name: recent blocks
entries.meaning: The last $\Crecenthistorylen$ blocks: each one's header hash, state root, accumulation-output root and the work packages reported in it. Guarantees must anchor to one of them.

entries.name: accumulation-output belt
entries.meaning: A Merkle mountain range (a compact append-only commitment) over the accumulation outputs of every block so far.

entries.name: last accumulation outputs
entries.meaning: The (service, hash) pairs that services yielded when they accumulated in the most recent block.

entries.name: Safrole state
entries.meaning: The block-production lottery's state, $(\pendingset, \epochroot, \sealtickets, \ticketaccumulator)$.

entries.name: pending validators
entries.meaning: The keys of next epoch's validators, fixed one epoch in advance so that tickets for that epoch can be made against them.

entries.name: ring root
entries.meaning: The Bandersnatch ring root of the pending validators' keys. A ticket proves that one of these validators made it without saying which.

entries.name: slot sealers
entries.meaning: Who may seal each slot of the current epoch: $\Cepochlen$ winning tickets, or, if not enough tickets were made, $\Cepochlen$ fallback Bandersnatch keys.

entries.name: ticket accumulator
entries.meaning: The best tickets submitted so far this epoch for the next epoch, kept sorted, at most $\Cepochlen$ of them.

entries.name: service accounts
entries.meaning: Every service, by its index: code hash, balance, storage, preimages and their requests, gas limits and so on.

entries.name: entropy
entries.meaning: Four 32-octet values: $\entropy_0$ accumulates fresh randomness from every block's VRF output; $\entropy_1$, $\entropy_2$, $\entropy_3$ are snapshots of it taken at the last three epoch changes.

entries.name: staging validators
entries.meaning: Validator keys (with metadata) queued to become pending at the next epoch change. Accumulation of the delegator service can replace them.

entries.name: active validators
entries.meaning: The validators of the current epoch: they author blocks, guarantee, assure and audit.

entries.name: previous validators
entries.meaning: The previous epoch's active validators, still needed to check guarantees and judgments made just before the epoch change.

entries.name: availability assignments
entries.meaning: For each core, at most one guaranteed work report waiting to become available, with the timeslot it was reported in.

entries.name: timeslot
entries.meaning: The timeslot of the most recent block. A slot is $\Cslotseconds$ seconds; an epoch is $\Cepochlen$ slots.

entries.name: privileged services
entries.meaning: The services with special powers: the manager $\manager$ (sets the privileges), the assigners $\assigners$ (one per core, set that core's authorizer queue), the delegator $\delegator$ (sets the staging validators), the registrar $\registrar$ (creates services with small reserved indices) and the always-accumulate services $\alwaysaccers$ with their gas.

entries.name: judgments
entries.meaning: What disputes have settled: the reports judged good $\goodset$, bad $\badset$ and unknowable $\wonkyset$, and the offending validators $\offenders$ (whose keys are then nulled out of new validator sets).

entries.name: statistics
entries.meaning: Activity counters: per validator for this epoch $\valstatsaccumulator$ and the last $\valstatsprevious$, per core $\corestats$ and per service $\servicestats$ for the latest block. Bookkeeping only: no other part of the transition reads them.

entries.name: ready queue
entries.meaning: Available work reports that cannot accumulate yet because a package they depend on has not accumulated, waiting at most an epoch, each with its unmet dependencies.

entries.name: accumulation history
entries.meaning: The hashes of the work packages accumulated in each of the last $\Cepochlen$ blocks, so that a package is not accumulated twice and dependencies can be checked.

sections.intro: A block $\block = (\header, \extrinsic)$ is a header and an extrinsic. The header's fields are written $\header_X$ with a capital letter; the extrinsic's five parts are written $\extrinsic_X$.

entries.name: block
entries.meaning: A header and an extrinsic.

entries.name: header
entries.meaning: The block's metadata, signed (sealed) by its author.

entries.name: parent hash
entries.meaning: The hash of the parent block's header.

entries.name: prior state root
entries.meaning: The Merkle root of the state before this block (the parent's posterior state).

entries.name: extrinsic hash
entries.meaning: A hash committing to the block's extrinsic.

entries.name: timeslot
entries.meaning: The block's timeslot; it becomes $\thetime'$ and must be later than $\thetime$.

entries.name: epoch marker
entries.meaning: Present only in the first block of an epoch: two entropy values and the Bandersnatch and Ed25519 keys of the next epoch's validators.

entries.name: winning-tickets marker
entries.meaning: Present only in the first block of an epoch at or past slot $\Cepochtailstart$ (when ticket submission has closed), and only if the accumulator is full: the next epoch's $\Cepochlen$ sealing tickets.

entries.name: offenders marker
entries.meaning: The Ed25519 keys of validators newly found to have misbehaved by this block's disputes.

entries.name: author index
entries.meaning: The block author's index in the active validator set $\activeset'$.

entries.name: entropy source
entries.meaning: A VRF signature by the author; its output is the block's contribution to the entropy $\entropy_0$.

entries.name: seal
entries.meaning: The author's Bandersnatch signature over the rest of the header, showing that the author holds the slot's ticket or is the slot's fallback key.

entries.name: extrinsic
entries.meaning: The block's payload of external data, in five parts.

entries.name: tickets
entries.meaning: Anonymous lottery tickets (ring-VRF proofs) for sealing slots of the next epoch, at most $\Cmaxblocktickets$ per block.

entries.name: preimages
entries.meaning: Data blobs that services had requested by hash, each with the requesting service's index.

entries.name: guarantees
entries.meaning: New work reports, each signed by two or three of the validators assigned to its core.

entries.name: assurances
entries.meaning: One signed bitfield per assuring validator: for each core, whether it holds its piece of that core's pending report's data.

entries.name: disputes
entries.meaning: Verdicts on work reports ($\xtverdicts$), with culprits ($\xtculprits$, guarantors of bad reports) and faults ($\xtfaults$, validators who judged a report the opposite way to its verdict).

entries.name: ancestor set
entries.meaning: The headers of the block's ancestors. Not part of the state: the model's importer is given the retained headers.

entries.name: newly available reports
entries.meaning: The work reports that this block's assurances made available; they go on to accumulation.

sections.intro: The paper writes types as blackboard-bold letters. Some reuse letters that usually mean something else in mathematics: $\workcontext$ is not the complex numbers and $\workreport$ is not the reals.

entries.name: validator key
entries.meaning: A validator's 336-octet key set: Bandersnatch key, Ed25519 key, BLS key and 128 octets of metadata.

entries.name: validator-set sizes
entries.meaning: The allowed sizes of a validator set: $3c$ for $2 \le c \le \Ccorecount$, that is a multiple of 3 from 6 to $3\Ccorecount$. In v0.8.1 the number of validators is not a fixed constant (there is no constant V).

entries.name: ticket
entries.meaning: A sealing-lottery ticket: its identifier (a VRF output) and its attempt number.

entries.name: service account
entries.meaning: One service's on-chain record: storage, preimages and requests, code hash, balance, gas limits for accumulation and transfers, and more.

entries.name: work package
entries.meaning: What a user submits to a core: an authorization token, the service and hash of the authorizer's code, the authorizer's configuration, a refinement context, and up to $\Cmaxpackageitems$ work items.

entries.name: work item
entries.meaning: One service's piece of a work package: the service, its code hash, a payload, gas limits for refinement and accumulation, the segments it imports, the extrinsic data it uses, and the number of segments it exports.

entries.name: refinement context
entries.meaning: The chain state a work package was refined against: a recent anchor block (its hash, state root and accumulation-belt root), a lookup-anchor block and its timeslot, and the packages it depends on.

entries.name: work report
entries.meaning: The result of refining a work package on a core: the availability specification, context, core, authorizer, one digest per work item, and more. It is what goes on chain.

entries.name: work digest
entries.meaning: One work item's result in a report: its service, code hash, payload hash, gas, the output or error, and usage counts.

entries.name: work error
entries.meaning: Why a work item produced no output: out of gas, a panic, a wrong number of exports, an over-size output, or code that was not available or too large.

entries.name: availability specification
entries.meaning: What makes a report's data checkable: the package hash, bundle length, erasure root, exports root and export count.

entries.name: guarantee
entries.meaning: A work report with a timeslot and the guarantors' signatures.

entries.name: operand tuple
entries.meaning: One work item's result, prepared as an input to its service's accumulation.

entries.name: deferred transfer
entries.meaning: A balance transfer with a memo, made by one service to another during accumulation and delivered to the receiver as an accumulation input.

entries.name: partial state
entries.meaning: The part of the state that accumulation may change: accounts, staging validators, authorizer queues and privileges.

entries.name: accumulation output
entries.meaning: What one service's accumulation returns: the new partial state, its transfers, an optional yielded hash, the gas used and the preimages it provides.

entries.name: implications
entries.meaning: The running context of an accumulation inside the PVM: the service, the partial state, the next new-service index, transfers, yield and provisions.

entries.name: segment
entries.meaning: A fixed-size block of exported data, $\Csegmentsize$ octets. Work items import and export segments.
entries.modelNote: no type of its own: segments are octet sequences of this length.

entries.name: hashes
entries.meaning: 32-octet values, usually hash outputs.
entries.modelNote: no type of its own: 32-octet sequences.

sections.intro: Uppercase Greek letters name the main functions.

entries.name: block transition
entries.meaning: The state transition: given the state and a block, the next state (or the block is invalid).

entries.name: state Merklization
entries.meaning: The Merkle root of the whole state; the next block's header carries it as $\H_\¬priorstateroot$.

entries.name: key nullifier
entries.meaning: Replaces the keys of known offenders in a validator set by the null key.

entries.name: sequential accumulation
entries.meaning: Accumulates a sequence of work reports in batches that fit the gas limit.

entries.name: parallel accumulation
entries.meaning: Accumulates one batch: every affected service once, combining their results.

entries.name: single-service accumulation
entries.meaning: Accumulates one service: gathers its inputs and runs its accumulate code.

entries.name: work-report computation
entries.meaning: Refines a work package on a core and builds its work report.

entries.name: historical lookup
entries.meaning: Looks up a preimage as it was available at a given past timeslot, so that refinement does not depend on the latest state.

entries.name: PVM
entries.meaning: The Polkadot Virtual Machine: runs a program until it halts, panics, runs out of gas, faults or calls the host.

entries.name: Is-Authorized invocation
entries.meaning: Runs a work package's authorizer code, in-core, to decide whether the package may use the core.

entries.name: Refine invocation
entries.meaning: Runs a service's refine code on one work item, in-core.

entries.name: Accumulate invocation
entries.meaning: Runs a service's accumulate code, on-chain, on its work results and transfers.

sections.intro: Inside the virtual machine the paper uses lowercase Greek letters for the machine's parts.

entries.name: registers
entries.meaning: The PVM's 13 64-bit registers. Its glyph is $\varphi$, drawn as an open loop; the authorizer queue uses the other phi, $\phi$.

entries.name: memory
entries.meaning: The PVM's RAM: a 32-bit address space in pages of $\Cpvmpagesize$ octets, each page inaccessible, read-only or writable.

entries.name: gas counter
entries.meaning: The gas left. Each instruction costs gas; running out stops the machine.
entries.modelNote: an argument and result of `PVM.psi`, not a declaration of its own.

entries.name: exit reason
entries.meaning: Why the machine stopped: halt, panic, out of gas, page fault or a host call.

sections.intro: Sans-serif capitals are protocol constants (values for the full chain; the test vectors use a smaller chain). Context strings ($\mathsf{X}$) and host-call gas costs ($\mathsf{M}$) are listed in the paper's index of notation.

entries.name: cores
entries.meaning: The number of cores: 341.

entries.name: epoch length
entries.meaning: The length of an epoch: 600 timeslots.

entries.name: slot period
entries.meaning: The length of a timeslot: 6 seconds.

entries.name: ticket-submission end
entries.meaning: The slot within an epoch at which ticket submission ends: 500.

entries.name: rotation period
entries.meaning: How often validators are reassigned to cores: every 10 timeslots.

entries.name: recent history length
entries.meaning: The number of recent blocks kept in $\recenthistory$: 8.

entries.name: authorizer pool size
entries.meaning: The most authorizers a core's pool holds: 8.

entries.name: authorizer queue size
entries.meaning: The number of entries in a core's authorizer queue: 80.

entries.name: assurance timeout
entries.meaning: The timeslots after which a reported but still unavailable report is dropped: 5.

entries.name: tickets per block
entries.meaning: The most tickets one block's extrinsic may carry: 16.

entries.name: items per package
entries.meaning: The most work items in a work package: 16.

entries.name: lookup-anchor age
entries.meaning: The oldest a work package's lookup anchor may be: 14,400 timeslots (a day).

entries.name: expunge period
entries.meaning: The timeslots after which an unreferenced preimage may be expunged: 19,200.

entries.name: accumulation gas per report
entries.meaning: The gas for one work report's accumulation: 47,000,000 (about 10 ms).

entries.name: Is-Authorized gas
entries.meaning: The gas for a work package's Is-Authorized code: 235,000,000 (about 50 ms).

entries.name: Refine gas
entries.meaning: The gas for a work package's Refine code: 23,500,000,000 (about 5 s).

entries.name: accumulation gas per block
entries.meaning: The total gas for all accumulation in one block: 16,450,000,000 (about 3.5 s).

entries.name: segment size
entries.meaning: The size of an exported segment: 4,104 octets.

entries.name: audit tranche period
entries.meaning: The seconds between audit tranches: 8.
